subject: Post-call: Veridium POC — acceptance evidence, SLOs & KPI playbook
messages:
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@veridium.ai>, Tom Barrett <tom.barrett@veridium.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Veridium POC scope & initial KPI playbook

Hi Hannah / Tom — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the things we aligned on, plus proposed next steps so we can get the POC kickoff scheduled.

Summary of scope (agreed):
- Duration: 2 weeks (pilot window), followed by 2-week optional extension for edge cases.
- Workloads: Conversational intent routing and automated summary generation across three internal customer channels (~100k tokens/day expected peak).
- Integration: API only (no on-prem deploy in phase 1).

Proposed acceptance criteria (high level):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 300ms for requests up to 512 tokens.
- Throughput: sustained 40–60 RPS during peak window with autoscale margin.
- Cost: target effective cost/token <= $0.0012; we’ll deliver token accounting per-session.
- Quality: intent-match >= 90% on your seed evaluation set; hallucination rate < 3% measured on the 120-sample audit set.

Owners we proposed on the call:
- Redwood AE / coordination: Vanessa Ortiz (me) — scheduling, deal & stakeholder alignment.
- Redwood SE / test plan & validation: Priyom Das — bench tests, instrumentation, runbook.
- Redwood performance lead: Rishi Malhotra — latency/throughput SLOs and fallback configs.
- Veridium: Hannah (product owner) & Tom (platform lead) — sample data, run windows, compliance constraints.

Attachments I’m sending with this email: a one-page KPI matrix and the proposed trial SLA (PDF). Priyom will follow up with the detailed test harness.

Next steps / ask list:
1) Hannah: confirm sample data delivery by EOD Fri (we need a ~120-record evaluation set + 6 10-min traffic traces).
2) Tom: confirm whether audit-logs & KMS integration are required for phase 1 or can be gated to a follow-on sprint.
3) Priyom/Rishi: draft performance test plan and a canary rollout for model variants by Thu.
4) Vanessa: propose two kickoff windows (Mon 30 Aug or Tue 31 Aug) — please confirm preferred date/time.

Thanks — I’ll move the HubSpot deal to PoC stage and share links once signed off.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: veridium_poc_kpi_matrix.xlsx, redwood_trial_sla.pdf

From: Tom Barrett <tom.barrett@veridium.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@veridium.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Veridium POC scope & initial KPI playbook

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

On data & compliance:
- We will share a masked subset of customer transcripts for validation; full PII redaction may still be in flight. Is it okay to run the POC on masked data hosted in Redwood's US region?
- We need audit logs for any access to raw traces; can Redwood surface those (request-level logging) within the trial window?

On KPIs:
- The 300ms p95 target looks aggressive for some of our longer responses; can we define a sequence-length bucket (e.g., <=128 tokens p95 180ms, 129–512 tokens p95 300ms)?

Schedule: Mon 30 Aug works for a kickoff — Tom + Hannah available 9–11am PT; prefer 10am if that fits your SE team.

Also, can you send the format we should use for the sample traces (CSV/JSON)? We want to make sure our engineering team sends the right shape.

—
Tom Barrett
Head of Platform, Veridium AI
Tom.Barrett@veridium.ai

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@veridium.ai>, Tom Barrett <tom.barrett@veridium.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Veridium POC scope & initial KPI playbook

Hi all — Priyom here. I put together the test-plan summary inline and attached a small sample trace format (veridium_sample_trace.json). Key points: 

1) Performance buckets (agree with Tom’s suggestion):
   - Short (<=128 tokens): target p95 <= 180ms; throughput target 80–100 RPS for short requests.
   - Medium (129–512 tokens): target p95 <= 300ms; throughput 40–60 RPS.
   - Long (>512 tokens up to 1024): no hard p95 SLA in this POC, but we’ll capture percentiles for visibility.

2) Test harness & metrics we’ll publish:
   - End-to-end latency (client -> Redwood -> model -> client), p50/p95/p99.
   - Token accounting & cost-per-session (we’ll provide both raw token counts and effective $/1k tokens).
   - Quality metrics: intent-match (micro-F1 against your labeled set), ROUGE-L for summary tasks, and a small human-audit sample for hallucination rate.

3) Runbook / workload schedule:
   - Day 0 (kickoff): baseline smoke, upload eval set, validate keys.
   - Day 1–3: dry-run with synthetic ramp to peak; capture warmup characteristics.
   - Day 4–10: 2 full days of peak-profile testing + 4 days of representative traffic sampling.
   - Final 2 days: regression checks and closed-loop hit-rate auditing.

4) Canaries & fallbacks:
   - We’ll roll a canary on a lower-capacity pool for the first 30 minutes of peak traffic. If p95 exceeds target by >20% for 15 continuous minutes, auto-fallback to an alternative model/quantized variant and record the delta.

What we need from Veridium:
- One 120-record labeled eval set (CSV or JSONL; attached sample is JSON lines).
- 3 anonymized 10-minute traffic traces (JSON) for realistic token distribution.
- Confirmation on KMS/audit-log requirement (bubble to Vanessa).

I’m attaching: veridium_sample_trace.json (trace shape) and will follow with a short script to run the harness against your sample data.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

Attachments: veridium_sample_trace.json

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@veridium.ai>, Tom Barrett <tom.barrett@veridium.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Veridium POC scope & initial KPI playbook

Thanks Tom — 10am PT on Mon 30 Aug works; I’ve sent a calendar invite with the agenda. Quick execution checklist and owners so everyone is aligned ahead of kickoff: 

Immediate owner checklist (who does what by when):
- Hannah: upload 120 labeled eval samples + 3 trace files by Fri 27 Aug EOD (owner: Veridium).
- Tom: confirm audit-log + KMS requirement (owner: Veridium). If you need KMS during phase 1 we’ll run an onboarding checklist (might push some items to gated tasks).
- Priyom: deliver the harness script and runbook before kickoff (owner: Priyom).
- Rishi: finalize the canary thresholds and fallback model config (owner: Rishi).
- Vanessa: finalize PoC kickoff agenda and HubSpot staging (owner: Vanessa).

Acceptance gates (must all be green for a successful POC):
- Data ingestion validated for sample set and traces.
- Baseline p95 latency meets bucketed targets (see Priyom’s buckets).
- Quality: intent-match >= 90% on labeled set AND hallucination <= 3% on the human audit sample.
- Cost: effective $/1k token below $1.20 (pilot target).

If any gate fails we’ll capture evidence, run one remediation iteration (up to 3 business days), and re-assess. If remediation fails for latency/throughput, we’ll exercise the fallback model and document divergence.

See you Monday at 10am PT — agenda, drive folder and HubSpot link are in the invite.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
